Practises repeating a deletion with dot one row at a time, as the instruction asks, so each row can be checked before the next goes; a single counted delete is shorter.
Practises how dot inherits the count of the change it repeats; the instruction asks for two equal deletions, and one larger delete would be shorter.
Practises giving dot a new count that replaces the remembered one; the instruction asks for that replacement, and a single word delete would be shorter.
Introduces the current-line address on an Ex command through join, whose effect is easy to see; Normal-mode J is shorter for two adjacent lines, and later exercises use ranges J cannot reach.
